reuse.why: The new expectedScheduleAmount builds on the existing worstCaseAmount and the matcher's getApproxNumberThreshold, so the tolerance comes from the same definition transaction matching uses.

duplication.why: Replaces five inline 'number ? value : worstCaseAmount(...)' dispatches with one shared function; only the pre-existing missing-amount (== null ? 0) checks are still repeated at api-models and the two schedules/app.ts sites.

placement.why: The expected-amount rule sits in shared/rules.ts next to worstCaseAmount and getApproxNumberThreshold, imported by the server consumers.

scope.why: Only the expected-amount computation, its callers, an optional _amountOp field on the forecast raw type and tests are touched.

maintainability.why: One function now owns the op-dependent expected amount; the untyped op string and the null case left outside the helper are small rough edges.

bypasses_abstraction.where: Every server site that computed the expected amount now calls expectedScheduleAmount.

disguised_duplication.where: None; the per-site dispatches are removed rather than reshaped.

one_place.where: expectedScheduleAmount in packages/loot-core/src/shared/rules.ts, called by api-models getExpectedAmount, budget schedule-template, forecast normalizeSchedule and schedules/app.ts updateActions and postTransactionForSchedule (the client display helper getScheduledAmount was already separate and is untouched).
